## {.tabset}

### Introduction

#### Column {width=100%}

```{python}
#| title: "Welcome to the EHR Multimorbidity Dashboard"

ui.markdown("""
## Interactive Data Visualization Platform

This dashboard provides comprehensive visualization and analysis tools for exploring multimorbidity
patterns and disease risk prediction models.

### Dashboard Capabilities

Once data is loaded, this dashboard will feature:

#### 1. Model Performance Analysis
- Compare predictive accuracy across different machine learning models
- Visualize performance metrics (AUC, accuracy, F1-score) by disease category
- Interactive filtering by disease type and model selection

#### 2. Variable Importance
- Explore key risk factors contributing to disease prediction
- Rank variables by importance scores
- Analyze feature contributions across different models

#### 3. Multimorbidity Network Analysis
- Visualize disease co-occurrence patterns
- Interactive network graphs showing disease relationships
- Cluster analysis of frequently co-occurring conditions

#### 4. Individual Risk Prediction
- Calculate personalized disease risk scores
- Interactive questionnaire for patient characteristics
- Real-time risk assessment with explanations

### Inspiration & Reference

This dashboard design is inspired by the [UKB-MDRMF Dashboard](https://luminite.shinyapps.io/ukb-mdrmf/),
which demonstrates sophisticated interactive visualization of multimorbidity data.

### Current Status

::: {.callout-note}
#### Development in Progress

The dashboard framework is now established and ready for data integration. Visualizations will be
populated as analysis progresses and datasets become available.

**Next Steps:**
- Prepare and load model performance data
- Integrate variable importance rankings
- Build disease co-occurrence networks
- Implement risk prediction models

Check back for updates as new interactive features are added!
:::

### Data Sources

When operational, this dashboard will utilize:

- **Electronic Health Records**: Large-scale EHR data from cohort studies
- **Machine Learning Models**: Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Networks
- **Disease Categories**: 21+ major disease groups
- **Predictor Variables**: Demographics, lifestyle, clinical measurements, genetic data

### Technical Framework

Built with:
- **Quarto**: Document and website generation
- **Shiny for Python**: Interactive server-side reactivity
- **Plotly**: High-quality interactive visualizations
- **pandas**: Data manipulation and analysis

### Questions or Feedback?

Visit our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/yourusername/EHR_website) to report issues,
suggest features, or contribute to the project.
""")
```

```{python}
#| title: "Example Chart Framework"

@render_plotly
def example_chart():
    """
    This demonstrates the Plotly charting framework.
    Replace with real data visualization when available.
    """

    # Placeholder data
    categories = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']
    values = [23, 45, 56, 78, 32]

    fig = go.Figure(data=[
        go.Bar(
            x=categories,
            y=values,
            marker_color='indianred',
            text=values,
            textposition='auto',
        )
    ])

    fig.update_layout(
        title="Example Bar Chart (Placeholder)",
        xaxis_title="Categories",
        yaxis_title="Values",
        template="plotly_white",
        height=400,
        annotations=[
            dict(
                text="This is a placeholder chart.<br>Real visualizations will appear when data is loaded.",
                xref="paper",
                yref="paper",
                x=0.5,
                y=0.5,
                xanchor="center",
                yanchor="middle",
                showarrow=False,
                font=dict(size=14, color="gray"),
                bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)",
                bordercolor="gray",
                borderwidth=1,
                borderpad=10
            )
        ]
    )

    return fig
```

```{python}
#| title: "Code Structure Example"

ui.markdown("""
### Implementation Pattern

When integrating real data, the code structure will follow this pattern:

```python
# 1. Load data
@reactive.Calc
def filtered_data():
    # Load dataset
    df = load_dataset()

    # Apply filters based on user inputs
    category = input.example_category()
    threshold = input.example_parameter()

    # Filter and process
    filtered = df[df['category'] == category]
    filtered = filtered[filtered['value'] >= threshold]

    return filtered

# 2. Create visualization
@render_plotly
def interactive_plot():
    # Get filtered data
    data = filtered_data()

    # Create Plotly chart
    fig = px.scatter(
        data,
        x='variable_x',
        y='variable_y',
        color='group',
        title="Dynamic Visualization"
    )

    return fig

# 3. Compute statistics
@render.text
def summary_stats():
    data = filtered_data()
    return f"Showing {len(data)} records"
```

This reactive pattern ensures visualizations update automatically when users change inputs.
""")
```
